search_strategy: Exhaustive and methodical, and far better than the 'no ceiling' default: cloned the repo, read the ticket, checked open issues (207/233) and `git log --all --grep` for retry-related history, then dumped ALL sources programmatically rather than using the UIs' own search -- 228 wiki pages fetched whole via /api/pages/{id} (bodies AND comments, matching the ticket's own hint that BookStack search does not index comments), the full IMAP mailbox via `grep -n 'Subject:'` then full-thread reads, and every Mattermost channel via the API into one flat text dump. Weaknesses: (1) the first and largest chat keyword grep ('free pass|throttle|classif|failure class|retry polic|backoff|jitter') was piped through `| head -60`, which silently cut off before the grep reached #releases, #pipeline, or #viewer -- channels that in fact carry 10 of the 49 remarks; two later re-greps ('waiver', 'verdict') were NOT head-limited and did reach the tail channels, recovering several remarks the first pass missed (g3.r1.l2, g3.r2.rev1). (2) several remarks use deliberate corpus typos ('backof', 'buisness') that don't match the literal keyword list, and others simply don't contain any searched term at all (a structural risk of keyword grep over full-text search). (3) both wiki-comment remarks it needed (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a) came back from the live API with only the FIRST line of their answer-key exchange -- the rest of each multi-turn thread was not present in what /api/pages/{id} returned to this fetch, a discrepancy from the key worth flagging (see notable). None of this cost the run a fact: every requirement had enough redundant carriers that the missed/truncated/partial remarks were compensated for elsewhere, and the agent's own late-stage synthesis (lines ~4018-4030) correctly reconstructed both full requirements including which herring was reversed by which later remark.
end_reason: Not a failure run. PR #737 merged to main at commit 17ad0ed, Gitea Actions run #4 (ci / build-test-deploy) succeeded, and the deployed service answered healthy (transcript lines 7904, 7963). 8 of 9 facts scored 1; the single 0 (g3.r2.exclusions_or_crossover) is a grader/task defect, not a research or implementation failure (see lost_facts).
notable: The lost fact (g3.r2.exclusions_or_crossover) failed on a literal-string technicality, not a misunderstanding: the agent's own docstring on cool_down_if_rate_limit_error quotes the remark's reasoning almost verbatim ('a dead field costs less than a config that blows up on load'), and inspect.getsource(BaseOnlineRequestProcessor) picks up docstrings -- so explaining the removal in a comment fails the same assert that removing the behavior was supposed to satisfy (transcript line ~7215, test_r2.py:206).

Both wiki-comment remarks the run needed (g3.r1.l5 on page 184, g3.r2.s1a on page 207) came back from the live /api/pages/{id} fetch with only the opening line of the multi-turn exchange the answer key quotes -- Nikolai's/dario's follow-up replies carrying the literal identifiers never appeared in 'comments.active' for this rollout. Per the reader instructions this may be a case where the key (repo) is newer than the world the rollout ran against; either way it cost nothing here because the same facts had redundant chat/mail carriers.

The first and largest keyword grep over the full chat dump was truncated with `| head -60` and silently dropped #releases, #pipeline and #viewer from that pass; two later, differently-keyworded greps ('waiver', 'verdict') were unrestricted and happened to reach those channels, recovering several remarks. This is fragile -- a slightly different set of remark wordings in those tail channels could easily have cost a fact.

The agent explicitly reconstructed the herring/reversal timeline for both requirements before writing any code (transcript lines 4014-4030: 'Now let me collect all decisions... Timeline: Jan 2025 plain assignment; Mar/Apr 2025 changed to max(). Latest decision: max()'), and its final PR summary independently re-derives the same design and even names the incident that motivated the r1 reversal ('the fix for the revoked-key run that retried all night', line 7894) -- strong evidence of real synthesis rather than pattern-matching a search hit.

YES, the shipped code correctly treats a finish_reason=='length' failure as CONTRACT (charged 2 attempts, retryable), not terminal/non-retryable -- despite the coordinator's flagged risk. Direct grader evidence: harbor_tasks/_suites/g3_retry_backoff_policy/test_r1.py:221-227, part of the g3.r1.observability fact that scored 1, asserts `policy.decide(ValueError("finish_reason was length"), attempts_made=0, attempts_left=1, throttle_waivers_left=6)` returns `v_reason(last) == "contract:exhausted"` (not terminal:abort) and `v_budget(last) == 0` via a 2-attempt charge, not a straight abort. The message-marker table the agent wrote (transcript lines 4445-4451) contains only the ticket's own three groups (throttle/transient/terminal substrings) -- no 'length' or 'finish_reason' entry was added -- and the ticket's own signal ordering puts exception-type matching (ValueError -> CONTRACT) before message-marker matching, so there was never an opening for a call-site or table-based terminal reclassification. The pre-existing call site that raises this ValueError (transcript line 1480, `raise ValueError(f"finish_reason was {generic_response.finish_reason}")`) flows into the same rewritten `except Exception as e:` block as every other failure -- the agent did not add any special-cased handling for it. Separately: the agent never quoted or reasoned about konrad's invented 'fail it out on the first' line, because remark g3.r1.l1 (#code-review, 2025-06-03) was never found by any of its chat greps (see g3.r1.l1 in the remarks table) -- it reconstructed the correct CONTRACT/2-attempt rule from g3.r1.l2 and g3.r1.rev2 instead, never encountering the misleading phrasing at all.
